reasons: Lake citations.official = '489 U.S. 602' (type 1, selected_official true); parallel array matches the frontmatter parallel_cite reporters exactly (109 S. Ct. 1402; 103 L. Ed. 2d 639; and the four specialty reporters).

Vendor-neutral '1989 U.S. LEXIS 1568' matches neutral_cite; opinion header renders '489 U.S. 602 (1989)' and 'Decided March 21, 1989'; identity expected_citation_found=true, canonical_name_match=true.

Kennedy majority upholds the FRA's mandatory suspicionless post-accident blood/urine testing under the special-needs balancing ('In limited circumstances, where the privacy interests implicated by the search are minimal ... a search may be reasonable despite the absence of such suspicion').
Marshall dissent confirms the disposition ('the majority holds that the need of the FRA ... outweighs any "minimal" intrusions'); holding paraphrase is faithful.
Frontmatter homes and the '## Appears on' section both declare [[Special Needs and Administrative Searches]] with role 'Key — Anchor', internally consistent.
Doctrinally sound: Skinner (with Von Raab) is the foundational special-needs suspicionless-search decision, so the anchor role is well-founded.
residual_risks: The target home page [[Special Needs and Administrative Searches]] is not inlined, so the reciprocal listing cannot be independently confirmed.
